title: 2010 AMC 8 Problem 10

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: Six pepperoni circles will exactly fit across the diameter of a \(12\)-inch pizza when placed as shown. If a total of \(24\) circles of pepperoni are placed on this pizza without overlap, what fraction of the pizza is covered by pepperoni?

solutions.text:
Each circle has \(\dfrac{1}{6} \) the diameter of the large circle, so it has \((\frac 16)^2 = \frac 1{36} \) of the total area.

Since there are \(24\) pepperoni, they take up \(24 \cdot \dfrac 1{36} = \frac 23 \) of the area.

Therefore, the answer is B .
hints: Area scales with the square of the diameter, then multiply by \(24\) pepperoni circles.
Six small diameters equal the pizza diameter.
